Historical findings CASEID FILE NOTE
1) Domain context: A generic institutional records office files ordinary paperwork by indexing each document to a unique identifier, storing the file in a dated folder, cross-referencing related records by field, and retaining the original copy with its access log.

2) What occurred: On a dated record, the actor created a duplicate document from a single ticket file. On a second dated record, the actor copied the duplicate document to three additional files. On a third dated record, the actor altered the barcode field in each copied file. On a fourth dated record, the actor altered the seat-number field in each copied file. On a fifth dated record, the actor set the issue-date field in each copied file to the original date. On a sixth dated record, the actor transmitted the copied files to three buyer accounts. On a seventh dated record, the actor directed each buyer account to present at the gate before the actor's own presentation. On an eighth dated record, the actor flagged the original record in the refund queue as settled. On a ninth dated record, the actor set the chargeback-status field in the account ledger to closed. On a tenth dated record, the actor cleared the identification-check field for each copied file.

3) Materials/access observed: The actor accessed the original ticket file in the records office archive. The actor accessed the buyer account ledger in the accounts database. The actor accessed the gate-scanner log in the venue channel. The actor used a document editor to modify the barcode field. The actor used a document editor to modify the seat-number field. The actor used a document editor to modify the issue-date field. The actor used a document editor to modify the chargeback-status field. The actor used a document editor to modify the identification-check field.

4) Indicators & artifacts: The records office file contains four ticket files with identical barcode field values but distinct file identifiers. The buyer account ledger shows three separate chargeback-status field entries set to closed on a single dated record. The gate-scanner log shows four scanner events with matching barcode field values within a dated time window. The refund queue shows the original record flagged as settled on a dated record. The account ledger shows the identification-check field cleared for each copied file on a dated record. The access log shows the actor account modifying the barcode field, seat-number field, issue-date field, chargeback-status field, and identification-check field in sequence on dated records.
